channel.description: Recent content in Tutorials on 梦兽编程

item.title: Why Rust Makes C++ Programmers Lose Sleep at Night: Lessons from My Migration Journey
item.description: A C++ developer with 5 years of experience shares real insights from switching to Rust. From memory safety to concurrency, these 10 features completely changed my perspective on systems programming

item.title: Capstone: stitching ten modules into one shippable image-intelligence agent
item.description: End-to-end delivery on ADK Go v2.4.0: a fetch → analyse → human-approval pipeline agent built with workflowagent plus Chain, a FunctionNode for the deterministic fetch, an AgentNode carrying an llmagent, a DynamicNode with ResumeOrRequestInput for HITL, RetryConfig for backoff, OutputKey to pass the brief, a postgres session service for persistence, loggingplugin and retryandreflect for cross-cutting concerns, telemetry.New for observability, universal.NewLauncher with authn.NewIdentityAwareProxy and authz.NewStrict for the web surface, and adkgo deploy cloudrun to publish it. All code passes go build and go vet.

item.title: Plugins and OpenTelemetry: 14 lifecycle hooks, early-exit semantics, and three fields nobody reads
item.description: The cross-cutting layer of ADK Go v2.4.0: the 14 hooks of plugin.Config and their four signature families, the early-exit and duplicate-name registration semantics of PluginManager, the implementation fact that CloseFunc and PluginConfig.CloseTimeout have no caller at all in v2.4.0, the three built-in plugins (loggingplugin with all twelve hooks, retryandreflect which injects failures back into the model, functioncallmodifier which rewrites the model-visible schema), the nine Options of telemetry.New with environment-driven exporters, the five span naming shapes, and the privacy asymmetry where tool arguments are reported unconditionally while conversation content needs an explicit environment variable.

item.title: Agent Registry and inbound authentication: the allow-all Noop defaults, and the risk of treating one header as an identity
item.description: The registry and authentication layers of ADK Go v2.4.0: the agentregistry client (ADC plus mTLS endpoint selection, quota project precedence, the All* iterators, the RemoteAgent/MCPToolset factories and the cleanName identifier rules); the four inbound authn implementations (Noop/Header/IAP/Custom) and the 401 versus 500 split; the CanActAsUser semantics of authz with its Noop/Strict pair; which routes are Public; which controllers never reach an authorizer at all; and the outbound auth package with ConsentRequiredError and its logging prohibitions.

item.title: Cross-language interoperability: the default-deny policy of `remoteagent.NewA2A` and its two metadata namespaces
item.description: agent/remoteagent/v2 and the server/adka2a metadata contract in ADK Go v2.4.0: the bidirectional adk_ and a2a: prefixed namespaces, the nine action fields that get carried across, the security rationale behind AllowTransferToAgent defaulting to false (a remote peer must not redirect local orchestration), the origin validation of agent cards and ErrUntrustedCardInterface, how aggregatePartial reassembles a peer's partial artifact chunks into a non-partial event, the text folding rule, RemoteTaskCleanupCallback defaulting to a 5-second cancel RPC, and the known gaps when interoperating with adk-python.

item.title: The A2A v2 server side: the Executor's nine event-mapping rules, and the Agent Card that generates itself
item.description: server/adka2a/v2 in ADK Go v2.4.0: the complete rules by which the Executor translates a session.Event into an a2a.Event (Submitted → Working → ArtifactUpdate{Append:true} → empty LastChunk → Completed/Failed/InputRequired), the two output modes OutputArtifactPerRun and OutputArtifactPerEvent, the coupling requirement between RunnerProvider and plugin installation, the exact trigger conditions of the four callbacks, why ADKExtensionURI is a metadata key rather than an Extensions.Activate call, how BuildAgentSkills derives skills from the agent tree, and the dual-protocol agent card produced by the a2a sub-launcher of the web launcher.

item.title: Containers, session storage and triggers: one session per delivery, and Pub/Sub redelivers once 429s are exhausted
item.description: The event-triggered deployment surface of ADK Go v2.4.0: the message contracts of the /apps/{app_name}/trigger/pubsub and /trigger/eventarc endpoints (base64 data, attributes merged in, CloudEvents structured versus binary modes), userID coming from the subscription or event.Source, one session per delivery with retries reusing it, 429 detection by error-string containment, exponential backoff with half jitter, a 500 after exhaustion so the upstream redelivers, ErrCompaction being logged without NACKing, the fact that the concurrency semaphore is never wired in the Pub/Sub controller, and why compaction is nearly pointless on the trigger surface.

item.title: The `adkgo` CLI: a command that only deploys, and the Dockerfile it generates for you
item.description: A complete tour of cmd/adkgo in ADK Go v2.4.0: it has only the deploy branch (two targets, cloudrun and agentengine, registered via blank imports), the Dockerfile cloudrun generates is distroless plus a CMD invoking web on the server port (so your entry point must accept the web subcommand), the relationship between the local authenticating proxy on 8081 and a2a_agent_url, the six switches --a2a/--api/--webui/--debug_api/--pubsub/--eventarc, agentengine's source archive upload and its three memory bank flags, and why there is no adk run / adk web / adk eval.

item.title: Chat UI and the wire protocol: /run, /run_sse, /run_live, and the Dev UI pieces ADK Go leaves unimplemented
item.description: The server/adkrest wire layer of ADK Go v2.4.0: how the three runtime endpoints differ (POST /run, POST /run_sse with its SSE frame format and write deadline, GET /run_live with WebSocket frames and a hardcoded LiveRunConfig), the strict decoding of RunAgentRequest and that functionCallEventId which is accepted but ignored, what a per-request Runner means, the DevPrefix=/dev/apps/{app_name} v2 API split, and the three feature areas deliberately answered with 501 (including why 404 would be wrong).

item.title: The three streaming layers: what Partial/TurnComplete really mean, the aggregator, and the half-contract that break discards
item.description: Streaming in ADK Go v2.4.0: the relationship between the model layer GenerateContent(ctx,req,stream bool), the event layer iter.Seq2, and the wire layer SSE/WebSocket; agent.StreamingMode exposing only none/sse with bidi hidden internally; what the LLMResponse.Partial note about the Runner fully processing only the final non-partial event implies; how streamingResponseAggregator buffers text, stitches thought signatures and rebuilds tool arguments from PartialArgs jsonPath; the full Event.IsFinalResponse() decision including why compaction events are excluded; and the subtle contract that compaction runs in a defer so early break still gets it.

item.title: Collaboration modes: chat / task / single_turn, and the tools the framework installs for your model
item.description: How llmagent.Config.Mode lands in ADK Go v2.4.0: installTaskTools attaching a same-named delegation tool on the parent according to each sub-agent's mode, ModeTask receiving its own finish_task, the delegation tool's Name/Description/Parameters all coming from the agent configuration, the do-not-call-in-parallel sentence hardcoded into the task tool description, DefersResponse and the synthesizeTaskFREvent detour, the different IncludeContents default for a single_turn node, and using the nine TestDelegation_* cases as the specification.

item.title: The three fixed orchestration agents: Sequential / Parallel / Loop, their implementation semantics and boundaries
item.description: The three agent/workflowagents packages in ADK Go v2.4.0: Config wraps a single agent.Config (LoopAgent adds MaxIterations uint), all three reject a custom Run, Sequential's fixed ordering and RunLive entry point, Parallel's errgroup plus <parent>.<child> branch naming and early-stop cancellation with teardown waiting, Loop's count==0 indefinite loop and Actions.Escalate exit, and where the selection boundary lies against the graph workflow engine.

item.title: Dynamic graphs and HITL: RunNode's seven options, the adk_request_input wire format, and resuming across requests
item.description: The two hardest pieces of the ADK Go v2.4.0 graph engine together: runtime orchestration with DynamicNode + RunNode (the seven With* options, failure classification, output delegation), the synthetic adk_request_input FunctionCall and LongRunningToolIDs produced by NewRequestInputEvent, the InterruptID uniqueness requirement (the Dev UI tracks answers by ID), the re-entry and handoff modes of RerunOnResume, the one-line ResumeOrRequestInput form, the idempotency semantics of Workflow.Resume and ErrNothingToResume, how ReconstructRunState rebuilds state from event history, and the hard limitation that parallel HITL is not supported.

item.title: Scheduler lifecycle and retries: seven node states, five backoffs, and a default that refuses to retry validation errors
item.description: The scheduling layer of the ADK Go v2.4.0 graph engine: the exact semantics of the seven NodeStatus values including the two causes of NodeWaiting, why NodeRunning must be re-scheduled after a restart and the two sources of NodeCancelled, what NodeState/RunState may and may not persist and how binary payloads are handled, DefaultRetryConfig's 5/1s/60s/2.0/full-jitter policy, the two exportable pure functions ShouldRetry and CalculateDelay, why ErrInputValidation is not retried by default, struct literal versus DefaultRetryConfig, plus concurrency caps and cancellation propagation (cancelAll/echoesCancellation/nil on sibling cancellation).

item.title: Routing and conditional execution: what Default really means, silent dead ends, and a deduplicated edge
item.description: Conditional execution in ADK Go v2.4.0: how the Route interface reads event.Routes, the exact matching rules of StringRoute/IntRoute/BoolRoute/MultiRoute/Default, the four scheduling semantics in findSuccessors (unconditional edges do not suppress Default, Default fires only when no concrete route matched, all-miss-without-Default is a silent dead end, same-target deduplication), the per-activation hard constraints (ErrMultipleOutputs/ErrMultipleRoutingEvents/ErrMultipleTerminalOutputs), the implicit behaviour that a FunctionNode must return *session.Event to carry routes, and branch derivation during fan-out.

item.title: Edges and the execution model: EdgeBuilder, the eight graph validations, and that single consumer goroutine
item.description: The wiring layer of the ADK Go v2.4.0 graph engine: Edge{From,To,Route} and the Start sentinel, EdgeBuilder's six methods plus Chain/Concat, the eight legality checks in workflow.New (duplicate edges, multiple default routes, unreachable nodes, unconditional cycles, sub-graph name collisions…), the consequences of name being RunState's persistence namespace and the graph-evolution risk, the one-goroutine-per-node plus single-consumer execution model, what yielding events in arrival order implies, and the userInput text concatenation rule.

item.title: All node types: Node's nine methods, six built-in nodes, and NodeConfig's tri-state pointers
item.description: The node layer of the ADK Go v2.4.0 graph engine: when each of the nine workflow.Node methods is called, BaseNode and custom nodes, the four constructors of the FunctionNode family (including FromState's parameter binding and the node_input escape hatch), EmittingFunctionFn, the constructors and semantics of AgentNode/ToolNode/JoinNode/WorkflowNode/ParallelWorker, and why the seven NodeConfig fields (ParallelWorker/RerunOnResume/WaitForOutput/RetryConfig/Timeout/EmitsOwnSpan) use pointers.

item.title: Context compaction: how to set the sliding window and tail retention, and what measured recall tells you about the cost
item.description: A deep dive into session/compaction in ADK Go v2.4.0: the trigger timing of the two strategies and constant-factor versus a genuine ceiling, a 60-turn measured comparison of prompt lengths, why recall is all-or-nothing, the verbatim Durable facts clause in the default prompt (measured 5 of 10 conversations losing everything versus 9 of 10 losing nothing), the escape hatch of putting unrecoverable facts in state, the five Config fields and Validate rules, ErrCompaction versus decline and failure, tail retention bypassing the plugin pipeline (required reading if you redact), and the launcher's process-wide constraint.

item.title: Events and platform: the three replaceable seams behind NewEvent(ctx,…)
item.description: The ADK Go v2.4.0 event model and the platform package: who writes and who reads each of the 12 fields once Event embeds model.LLMResponse, the two orthogonal history-visibility rules of Branch and IsolationScope, the seven fields of EventActions including the framework-exclusive Compaction, why NewEvent(ctx,…) must take a ctx, and how the platform.Now / NewUUID / RunTasks seams enable deterministic replay and concurrency-controlled tests.

item.title: Session and State: three prefixes, one delta merge, and a storage contract you can test
item.description: The full ADK Go v2.4.0 session layer: the real signatures of session.Session/State/Events, the app:/user:/temp: state scopes, how StateDelta reaches storage via AppendEvent and strips temporary keys, the {var}/{var?}/{artifact.file} placeholder rules in instructions, the session/database (GORM) and vertexai persistence options, the sessiontestsuite conformance suite, and where the artifact and memory sibling services begin and end.

item.title: SkillToolset: turning a SKILL.md directory into capability the agent loads on demand
item.description: A complete tour of tool/skilltoolset in ADK Go v2.4.0: the five methods of skill.Source and its sentinel errors, NewFileSystemSource(fs.FS), the two preload modes (WithCompletePreloadSource / WithFrontmatterPreloadSource) and the reload closure, merging several sources with NewMergedSource, the SKILL.md frontmatter specification (including both allowed-tools spellings), and the three automatically injected tools list_skills/load_skill/load_skill_resource plus the XML inventory injected by ProcessRequest.

item.title: Tool confirmation (HITL): is one flag enough, or should you take over the protocol?
item.description: The two-gear tool confirmation design in ADK Go v2.4.0: declarative RequireConfirmation / RequireConfirmationProvider / tool.WithConfirmation versus the manual ctx.ToolConfirmation() + ctx.RequestConfirmation(hint, payload); the adk_request_confirmation protocol contract (the FunctionResponse must carry the same id, the same name, and confirmed), toolconfirmation.OriginalCallFrom parsing, idempotent re-entry and how to use FunctionCallID.

item.title: The MCP Toolset: Transport/Endpoint/Auth wiring and self-healing disconnects
item.description: A complete tour of tool/mcptoolset in ADK Go v2.4.0: the seven fields of mcptoolset.New(Config) and their mutual-exclusion rules, an in-memory MCP server for tests, the Endpoint shortcut for streamable HTTP, the auth.CredentialProvider versus OAuthHandler fight over the Authorization header, connectionRefresher retry semantics, plus toolset trimming and confirmation policies.

item.title: Function tools and streaming tools: functiontool.New, every Config field, and the context available inside a tool
item.description: The foundation of the ADK Go v2.4.0 tool layer: functiontool.New's generic Func[TArgs,TResults] signature, automatic schema inference (jsonschema rather than genai.Schema), NewStreaming returning iter.Seq2[string,error], the real semantics of IsLongRunning, what a tool can do through agent.Context, and the official agenttool workaround for the Google Search plus function tool conflict.

item.title: Module 10: Production Hardening (ADK Go 2.x)
item.description: agentregistry with authn/authz, the plugin system and OpenTelemetry observability, the capstone and evaluation strategy (including the fact that there is no eval package on the Go side)

item.title: The launcher family: which of console / web / full / prod / universal / agentengine to pick
item.description: A complete map of ADK Go v2.4.0 runtime entry points: the Launcher and SubLauncher interfaces, Config.Validate, universal's default sub-launcher rule, how full and prod compose, web's api/webui/a2a/pubsub/eventarc keywords, the default open authn/authz, and h2c — with a selection decision table and a troubleshooting list.

item.title: Module 9: A2A and Cross-Language Interoperability (ADK Go 2.x)
item.description: server/adka2a and the v2 protocol implementation, remoteagent for consuming remote agents, the agent card origin pinning fix, and version alignment with the Python/Java/Kotlin/TypeScript ADKs

item.title: Three routes to Hello World, and wiring up a model: launcher, runner, workflowagent
item.description: Getting started with ADK Go v2.4.0: one line with the launcher, driving the event stream directly with the runner (iter.Seq2), or starting with a graph via workflowagent. Every llmagent.Config field is covered — Instruction templates, GlobalInstruction, OutputSchema injection, the Mode default that changes with position — plus the gemini/openaimodel/apigee model layer.

item.title: Module 8: Deployment and Operations (ADK Go 2.x)
item.description: adkgo deploy (cloudrun/agentengine), containerisation, the web launcher with pubsub/eventarc triggers, the prod launcher, and how authentication lands

item.title: The unified agent.Context: the single most important type in 2.x
item.description: ADK Go 2.x merged ToolContext and CallbackContext into agent.Context. This article walks its capability surface method by method against the v2.4.0 source: the invocation / agent call / step terminology, State/Actions/SearchMemory/RequestConfirmation, the parallel-isolation semantics of Branch and IsolationScope, the StrictContextMock testing pattern, and four anti-patterns.

item.title: Module 7: Streaming and Multimodal (ADK Go 2.x)
item.description: SSE and event streams, partial event handling, two-way audio (bidi/live), streaming function tools, and Chat UI integration

item.title: Module 6: New Multi-Agent Patterns (ADK Go 2.x)
item.description: The new behaviour of the workflowagents trio on top of the graph engine, plus llmagent's chat/task/single_turn collaboration modes and structured input/output

item.title: Module 5: The Graph Workflow Engine (core of ADK Go 2.x)
item.description: A complete tour of the workflow package: node types, Chain/EdgeBuilder/fan-out-join, routing, concurrent scheduling with per-node retry and timeouts, and HITL pause/resume with dynamic graphs

item.title: Module 4: Sessions, Events and Context Compaction (ADK Go 2.x)
item.description: The session/state trio, NewEvent(ctx) and platform providers, session/compaction context compression and recall, and the database session service

item.title: 2.x Project Layout and go.mod Conventions: Making an ADK Go Project Maintainable by a Team
item.description: Directory conventions for the ADK Go v2.4.0 era, go.mod and toolchain pinning, using go.work during v1/v2 coexistence, standalone submodules (plugin/agentanalytics), how to split graphs and tools into packages, testdata goldenfiles, and CI conventions.

item.title: Module 3: The Tool System (ADK Go 2.x)
item.description: functiontool and streaming function tools, the MCP toolset, tool confirmation for human approval, and the SkillToolset skill directory

item.title: Installing and Verifying ADK Go 2.x: go get /v2, the adkgo CLI, and your first working agent
item.description: Install ADK Go v2.4.0 from scratch: the Go 1.27.1 toolchain, go get google.golang.org/adk/v2, credential setup (Gemini API key / Vertex ADC), the adkgo deployment CLI versus how the launcher actually runs your agent, with a full verification checklist and a failure triage table.

item.title: Module 2: The Core Object Model (ADK Go 2.x)
item.description: The unified agent.Context, platform providers, Hello World and gemini.NewModel(ctx), the launcher family and how you actually run an agent

item.title: Module 1: Environment and Project Layout (ADK Go 2.x)
item.description: Setting up ADK Go v2.4.0: go get adk/v2, the adkgo CLI, credential configuration, how the launcher runs, and the /v2-era go.mod and directory conventions

item.title: The Go Toolchain Floor: Why ADK Go 2.x Needs 1.26.6+, and the Go 1.26/1.27 Changes That Actually Affect Agent Code
item.description: ADK Go v2.4.0 requires go 1.26.6 in go.mod. This article explains how that enforcement works, the GOTOOLCHAIN traps behind restrictive networks, and the Go 1.26/1.27 changes that genuinely matter for agent code: new(expr), generic methods, Green Tea GC, the goroutineleak profile, the asynctimerchan removal, and the stdversion check.

item.title: Migrating 1.x → 2.x in Practice: Module Path, agent.Context, NewEvent(ctx)
item.description: A complete hands-on migration of ADK Go from 1.x to 2.x: go.mod and toolchain, import rewriting, adding ctx to session.NewEvent, agent.Context unification with StrictContextMock, rewriting orchestration as a graph, per-package verification and rollback strategy.

item.title: What ADK Go 2.0 Brings: the v0.2 → v1.7 → v2.4 Change Map
item.description: A major-version change map verified against the google/adk-go v2.4.0 source tree: the graph workflow engine, the three collaboration modes, the unified agent.Context, the adkgo CLI rename, and the Go 1.26.6 floor.

item.title: Module 0: Versioning and Migration (ADK Go 2.x)
item.description: The ADK Go 2.0 change map, hands-on 1.x→2.x migration, and why the toolchain floor is Go 1.26.6+

item.description: A brand-new series built on Google ADK Go v2.4.0: the graph workflow engine, collaboration modes, the unified agent.Context, built-in human-in-the-loop, SkillToolset, and context compaction. 31 articles, from zero to production.

item.title: A 1000x Gap: How Google Used Rust to Push Memory-Safety Bugs Below 20% — and the Playbook You Can Copy
item.description: In 2025 Google disclosed that memory-safety vulnerabilities on Android fell below 20% for the first time, and Rust code carries roughly 1000x fewer memory-safety bugs per million lines than C/C++. This article breaks down why, shows a C/Rust use-after-free comparison, and gives an actionable checklist.

item.title: Ditch Arduino: Write Microcontrollers in Rust + Embassy — Blink an LED and Learn Async Bare-Metal Programming
item.description: Arduino uses C++, where a few dozen KB of RAM means array overruns and dangling pointers slip past the compiler. This guide gets you running Rust bare-metal (no_std) plus the Embassy async framework on a Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040): toolchain, Cargo.toml, memory.x, an async blink, and 5 beginner pitfalls.

item.title: Stop Hand-Rolling JWT Validation: Add Production-Grade Auth to Your Rust API with OIDC + Axum
item.description: Rolling your own JWT validation, 8 out of 10 people miss something: no alg=none guard, no aud/iss checks, hardcoded keys, no clock-skew tolerance. This guide builds an OIDC Bearer-token validation middleware in Axum — JWKS fetching, algorithm whitelist, iss/aud checks, clock-skew tolerance — plus the simplest way to plug into Keycloak or Auth0.
